newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission faces battle over arable aid cuts.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission faces battle over arable aid cuts.

text.p: European farmers could be hit by cuts in export refunds if proposals to help beef producers using savings in aid to cereal farmers do not go through, an European Union (EU) official said on Wednesday.

"The European Commission is facing solid opposition over its plan to cut aid to cereal farmers to finance support for beef producers hit by mad cow disease but they are warning that export refunds could be hit," the official told Reuters.

"There was no discussion on the plan to cut cereal aids at Tuesday's special agriculture committee which discussed proposals for beef sector aid, but it is clear that there is a wide gulf between member states over taking money from the arable sector for extra aid to beef.
"There is certainly a blocking minority," the official added.
The Commission is ready to postpone a decision on cuts in arable area aid and set-aside compensatory payments at the meeting of EU farm ministers in Luxembourg on Monday, a senior official said.
"The most important issue will be to get a deal on beef aid," the official said.
EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler is proposing to cut arable area aid payments and set-aside compensation to help finance aid to beef producers hit by the mad cow crisis.
A proposal approved by the Commission which is due to be put to next week's meeting aims to cut aid on cereals by seven percent, equivalent to two percent of the turnover (price of cereals plus aid).
Set-aside compensatory payments would be cut by 27 percent, Commission officials say.
The European Parliament has so far not given its opinion on the Commission's package of beef aid measures which include the planned aid cuts to the cereal sector.

"This means that ministers may not be willing to take a decision because the parliament is sensitive about so-called 'political decisions' agreed before MEPs give an opinion," a Commission official said.

By January the European Union will have 600,000 tonnes of beef in store as a result of BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) and Commission officials put the cost of market intervention and aid to producers at 26 billion Ecus.

"We are confident that we will eventually get the proposed cereal cuts through. If we don't there will have to be cuts in export refunds and that will hit farmers' pockets much more," another official said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
